stem: Iodates are compounds that contain the $\text{IO}_3^-$ anion.

parts.label: (a)
(b)
parts.text:
The reaction of iodine and hot aqueous sodium hydroxide is similar to that of chlorine and hot aqueous sodium hydroxide. Sodium iodate, $\text{NaIO}_3$, is formed as one of the products.

Suggest an equation for the reaction of iodine and hot aqueous sodium hydroxide.

parts.label: (c)(i)
parts.stem:
The decomposition of hydrogen peroxide, $\text{H}_2\text{O}_2$, is catalysed by acidified $\text{IO}_3^-$.

$\text{H}_2\text{O}_2$ reduces acidified $\text{IO}_3^-$ as shown.

$$5\text{H}_2\text{O}_2 + 2\text{H}^+ + 2\text{IO}_3^- \rightarrow \text{I}_2 + 5\text{O}_2 + 6\text{H}_2\text{O}$$

This reaction is followed by the oxidation of $\text{I}_2$ by $\text{H}_2\text{O}_2$.

| half-equation | $E^\ominus/\text{V}$ |
| :--- | :--- |
| $\text{H}_2\text{O}_2 + 2\text{H}^+ + 2\text{e}^- \rightleftharpoons 2\text{H}_2\text{O}$ | +1.77 |
| $\text{IO}_3^- + 6\text{H}^+ + 5\text{e}^- \rightleftharpoons \frac{1}{2}\text{I}_2 + 3\text{H}_2\text{O}$ | +1.19 |
| $\text{O}_2 + 2\text{H}^+ + 2\text{e}^- \rightleftharpoons \text{H}_2\text{O}_2$ | +0.68 |
parts.text:
Use the data to show that the separate reactions of $\text{H}_2\text{O}_2$ with $\text{IO}_3^-$ and with $\text{I}_2$ are both feasible under standard conditions.

In your answer, give the equation for the reaction of $\text{H}_2\text{O}_2$ with $\text{I}_2$.

parts.label: (c)(ii)
parts.text: Write the overall equation for the decomposition of $\text{H}_2\text{O}_2$ catalysed by acidified $\text{IO}_3^-$.

parts.label: (d)(i)
parts.stem:
A student collects some data for the reaction of $\text{H}_2\text{O}_2$ with acidified $\text{IO}_3^-$, as shown in the table.

| experiment | $[\text{H}_2\text{O}_2]/\text{mol dm}^{-3}$ | $[\text{IO}_3^-]/\text{mol dm}^{-3}$ | $[\text{H}^+]/\text{mol dm}^{-3}$ | initial rate of reaction/$\text{mol dm}^{-3}\text{s}^{-1}$ |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 1 | 0.0500 | 0.0700 | 0.025 | $1.47 \times 10^{-5}$ |
| 2 | 0.100 | 0.0700 | 0.050 | $2.94 \times 10^{-5}$ |
| 3 | 0.100 | 0.140 | 0.025 | $5.88 \times 10^{-5}$ |
| 4 | 0.150 | 0.140 | 0.025 | $8.82 \times 10^{-5}$ |
parts.text:
Use the data to determine the order of reaction with respect to $[\text{H}_2\text{O}_2]$, $[\text{IO}_3^-]$ and $[\text{H}^+]$.

Show your reasoning.

parts.label: (d)(ii)
parts.text: Use your answer to (d)(i) to write the rate equation for this reaction.

parts.label: (d)(iii)
parts.text:
Calculate the value of the rate constant, $k$, using data from experiment 4 and your answer to (d)(ii).

Give the units of $k$.

parts.label: (e)(i)
parts.stem:
$\text{Pb}(\text{IO}_3)_2$ is only sparingly soluble in water at $25^\circ\text{C}$.

The solubility product, $K_{\text{sp}}$, of $\text{Pb}(\text{IO}_3)_2$ is $3.69 \times 10^{-13} \text{ mol}^3\text{dm}^{-9}$ at $25^\circ\text{C}$.
parts.text: Write an expression for the solubility product of $\text{Pb}(\text{IO}_3)_2$.

parts.label: (e)(ii)
parts.text: Calculate the solubility, in $\text{mol dm}^{-3}$, of $\text{Pb}(\text{IO}_3)_2$ at $25^\circ\text{C}$.

parts.label: (f)(i)
parts.stem:
$\text{NH}_4\text{IO}_3$ is an unstable compound that readily decomposes when warmed. The decomposition reaction is shown.

$$\text{NH}_4\text{IO}_3(\text{s}) \rightarrow \frac{1}{2}\text{N}_2(\text{g}) + \frac{1}{2}\text{O}_2(\text{g}) + \frac{1}{2}\text{I}_2(\text{g}) + 2\text{H}_2\text{O}(\text{l}) \quad \Delta H = -154.6 \text{ kJ mol}^{-1}$$
parts.text:
Use the data in the table to calculate the entropy change of reaction, $\Delta S$, of the decomposition of $\text{NH}_4\text{IO}_3(\text{s})$.

| compound | $S/\text{J K}^{-1}\text{mol}^{-1}$ |
| :--- | :--- |
| $\text{NH}_4\text{IO}_3(\text{s})$ | 42 |
| $\text{N}_2(\text{g})$ | 192 |
| $\text{O}_2(\text{g})$ | 205 |
| $\text{I}_2(\text{g})$ | 261 |
| $\text{H}_2\text{O}(\text{l})$ | 70 |

parts.label: (f)(ii)
parts.text:
This reaction is feasible at all temperatures.

Explain why, using the data in (f) and your answer to (f)(i).
